baseline_definition: Mean FPD of the 2013-2015 vintages = 0.014%. Earliest three vintages that are both fully observed and drawn from the post-GFC at-scale business.
rationale: FPD is the earliest observable signal of underwriting or fraud deterioration: a borrower who never pays once cannot be explained by anything that happened after origination. Ratio to baseline rather than an absolute level, because the absolute rate (~0.07%) is too small to set a meaningful fixed line on.
provenance: ILLUSTRATIVE thresholds. The 2x/3x lines are our judgement. The baseline window is documented but is also a choice - 2012 and earlier are a materially different business (603 loans in 2007 vs 320,419 in 2017).

baseline_definition: Each grade's own mean MOB-12 cumulative default across the 2013-2015 vintages. Computed per grade, so each grade is judged against itself.
rationale: Closes the control gap in L-04 / L-07, which are denominated in grade and assume the label's meaning is constant. It is not: within-grade MOB-12 default rose 31.8-36.9% from baseline by the 2016 vintage while the grade MIX stayed roughly stable. A limit denominated in a rating needs the rating's meaning monitored separately or it measures a label, not a risk.
provenance: ILLUSTRATIVE thresholds. The 20%/30% lines are our judgement. The mechanism (drift measured within grade against the grade's own baseline) is not - it is what removes the mix confound that inverted the macro correlation in challenge-04.

baseline_definition: Mean MOB-12 cumulative default of the 2013-2015 vintages, 36-month loans.
rationale: The slow confirmatory indicator. Included deliberately alongside E-01 to show the lag: this one cannot speak about the 2018 vintage at all - the cohort is not observed to MOB 12 - while FPD already reads its highest ever. An EWI framework needs both, and needs to know which is which.
